Camila / Samir / Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask. Confirming details below that we can include in the SOW/SLA. I’m copying Marcus for the ops/billing wording.

Isolation model (what we will commit to):
- Logical pool fencing: BrightRelay reserved pool will be provisioned as a tenant-scoped dedicated pool. Scheduling is tenant-aware; workloads from other customers are not scheduled on the same tenant namespace.
- Node allocation: GPUs backing the reserved pool are drawn from a pool of nodes whose scheduler enforces node-level allocation so that BrightRelay workloads are only placed on nodes assigned to BrightRelay's tenant namespace. This prevents cross-tenant GPU sharing at runtime.
- KV cache & prefix caching: Per-tenant caches are enforced; cache shards are not shared across tenants to avoid state leakage and noisy-cache eviction.
- Network & keys: We support VPC peering/endpoint for network isolation. Customer-managed KMS integration is supported; logs and metadata can be restricted per contract so they do not transit public shared systems.

Performance & SLA (suggested language):
- Baseline: Redwood guarantees a committed baseline throughput for BrightRelay's reserved pool of 35 RPS (64-token average request) with a 95th-percentile tail latency <= 120ms.
- Burst: The reserved pool includes up to 20% burst capacity above committed throughput. Burst is available for short windows and is billed at the agreed burst rate in the SOW.
- Autoscale behavior: Autoscaling to provision additional nodes for the reserved pool is triggered automatically when 90% of committed capacity is sustained for 30s; typical provisioning time is 90–180s depending on model size.
- Exceptions & maintenance: Scheduled maintenance windows (48h notice) and force-majeure events are excluded from SLA credit calculations. Software regressions with prior notice are treated as planned maintenance unless an outage is reported.

Suggested contract clause (1–2 sentences):
"Redwood will provision a tenant-scoped reserved GPU pool for BrightRelay. The pool will be logically fenced such that compute scheduling, KV cache shards, and model-serving namespaces are exclusive to BrightRelay; Redwood will not schedule other customers' workloads on BrightRelay-assigned nodes. Redwood guarantees a baseline throughput of 35 RPS (64-token average) with 95th-percentile tail latency <= 120ms, subject to the exceptions described in the SOW."

Attachments: SLA-draft-BR-8721-20261109.pdf (redlines included), reserved-pool-diagram.png (deployment/topology).

If that wording looks good I can hand it to Legal to bake into the SOW. Marcus — please advise on billing language for burst usage and how we present credit calculations.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
